text:
aisha: quick question — we're doing a canary to shift traffic from the NLB to ALB for `embed-service` (tls at edge). I set up the ALB target group and a 10% weight via terraform but readiness probes are failing for the ALB targets. anyone seen this?

mike: what do your service & ingress/gateway args look like? Common culprits: wrong targetType (instance vs ip), nodePort mismatch, or healthcheck path/port not reachable behind ALB.

jen: fwiw we had similar with `targetType = ip` and pod uses hostPort. ALB expects IP targets that directly receive traffic; if service is NodePort->Node you need instance targets.

omar: can you paste the service YAML + ALB target group health check config? also any tls termination config (alb annotation `alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/load-balancer-attributes` etc)?

 aisha: pasted snippet: ```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: embed-service
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "nlb"
spec:
  type: NodePort
  ports:
    - port: 443
      targetPort: 8443
      protocol: TCP
  selector:
    app: embed
```

 aisha: terraform for alb target group: `target_type = "ip"`, health_check { path = "/healthz" port = "traffic-port" protocol = "HTTPS" } and ALB is configured to terminate TLS.

mike: immediate issue: your k8s svc annotation is still `nlb`. ALB controller won't attach if svc annotation tells AWS to create an NLB. For ALB you need an Ingress/Gateway API resource (ALB Ingress controller) or change flow to NodePort + NLB instance targets. Mixing annotations will confuse provisioning.

jen: also targetPort=8443 — but health_check is hitting `traffic-port` which maps to 443 on the TG. ALB will connect to pod IP:8443 if target_type=ip, that is fine — but are pods listening on 8443 for plaintext or expecting TLS? If ALB terminates TLS, backend protocol should be HTTP or HTTPS? If ALB -> pods is HTTPS you need proper certs and SNI, otherwise ALB health check over HTTPS may fail.

omar: try one quick experiment: 1) change service annotation to remove NLB tag (or add correct ALB annotations), 2) ensure Ingress or Gateway API is creating ALB TGs for the service (we use alb-ingress-controller in this cluster), 3) for canary set TG weights in terraform but verify TG health manually.

 aisha: hmm we use Gateway API with aws-load-balancer-controller v2.4. I mistakenly left the nlb annotation from a prior test. ok removing that. What do I set on the service for Gateway->pod comms?

mike: with Gateway API you usually keep Service as ClusterIP (no k8s LB) and the AWS controller will create target groups pointing to pod IPs if you annotate the Service or use the Service-backed references. So switch Service type to ClusterIP and make sure gateway/listener rules are correct. Example minimal svc: ```yaml
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  ports:
    - name: https
      port: 8443
      targetPort: 8443
```

jen: health checks: ALB health check path /healthz must be served on 8443 and respond with 200. If your pod only serves mTLS on that port (client cert required), ALB health probe will fail unless you allow probe without cert or use TLS HEALTHCHECK with proper cert options. We had a trick: expose a plaintext /ready endpoint on a different port for ALB healthchecks and use TG health_check.port = "31234" or set protocol to HTTP on an HTTP-only endpoint.

omar: terraform tip: when creating aws_lb_target_group set `port = 8443` and `protocol = "HTTPS"` if backend expects TLS, and add `health_check { matcher = "200" }` and `health_check_protocol = "HTTPS"`. If you terminate TLS at ALB and talk HTTP to pod, use `protocol = "HTTP"` and ensure ALB->pod traffic isn't expecting TLS.

 aisha: deploy-bot: Canary created: tg/canary-embed weight 10% -> prod-tg weight 90% :white_check_mark:

mike: after removing nlb annotation what did the controller create? any error in controller logs? `kubectl -n kube-system logs deployment/aws-load-balancer-controller` will show failures to register targets.

 aisha: got it — controller logs showed `skipping service: service is annotated as nlb`. after removing the annotation new TGs show up and targets register, but health shows unhealthy because of TLS handshake errors.

jen: TLS handshake = ALB->pod expects TLS. If ALB terminates TLS you should configure backend protocol to HTTP. So either: (A) ALB terminates TLS and backend is HTTP (change pod to serve plaintext or add sidecar), or (B) keep TLS end-to-end: ALB uses HTTPS to pods and you manage certs on pods (not ideal). We usually pick A and use internal plaintext on port 8080/8443 with network policy restricting access.

omar: small config snippet we used to allow ALB healthcheck on a non-TLS endpoint: ```terraform
resource "aws_lb_target_group" "embed" {
  port = 8080
  protocol = "HTTP"
  health_check {
    path = "/healthz"
    matcher = "200"
  }
}
```

 aisha: plan: change svc -> ClusterIP, expose pod on 8080 for HTTP health only, update TG/ALB backend to HTTP:8080 in terraform, keep ALB listener for 443 TLS -> forward to TG. will open PR.

mike: ping me on the PR — we should also add gateway listener rule for canary weight and a rollback plan (flip weights in terraform).

jen: also add note to run `kubectl port-forward` to one pod and test `curl -k https://localhost:8443/healthz` or `curl http://localhost:8080/healthz` to validate both paths before applying.

 aisha: will do. thanks all :rocket:
